LESSON: CLOTHING CONSTRUCTION PROCESSES ● SEAMS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: HOME SCIENCE
Strand: Clothing and Textiles
Topic 3.4: Clothing Construction Processes ● Seams
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Clothing Construction Processes ● Seams, part of Clothing and Textiles in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 HOME SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How can seams be creatively used in clothing construction? 2. How do you determine the seam to use in clothing construction?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the meaning of a seam. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to share their views,

2. search for information from print media, electronic devices, discuss with peers and present in class on types of seams, Inconspicuous seams- open, French, Conspicuous seams-overlaid and double stitched seams Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted digital devices with appropriate accessibility features. Screen resolutions could be adjusted for learners who are sensitive to light and colour,

3. watch video clips or demonstrations from the teacher 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on the meaning of a seam. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to share their views,
2. search for information from print media, electronic devices, discuss with peers and present in class on types of seams, Inconspicuous seams- open, French, Conspicuous seams-overlaid and double stitched seams Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted digital devices with appropriate accessibility features. Screen resolutions could be adjusted for learners who are sensitive to light and colour,
3. watch video clips or demonstrations from the teacher 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Clothing Construction Processes ● Seams together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: When learners reflect on their own work of the seams made and adjust accordingly.

● Self-efficacy: The learner shows a concerted attention to details while making the seams.

Values:
● Love: Learners portray a caring attitude when sharing the limited resources in the Home science workshop.

● Responsibility: The learner observes care of tools and equipment in the Hom science workshop and when carefully

disposing clippings and chippings from the fabrics and threads during stitching.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental conservation: Learners dispose of scraps of fabrics and threads appropriately during stitching.

● Life skills: analytical and critical thinking when following procedures of making seams.

Suggested learning resources:

Relevant textbooks, charts, video clips, adapted home science laboratory, adapted digital devices, adapted sewing tools

and equipment, fabric,
